c3620ac29bf55cec7fec6e86cac4a1249561f932: Rosswald is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 9 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Rosswald's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. With a summit at 2536 m and a village at 1820 m, Rosswald's snow cover is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strains early in the season, but conditions recover quickly with the first heavy snowfalls. Staying in Rosswald is clearly on the pricier side: a 52€ day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but it's worth being aware of it before you go. In short: Rosswald doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

c3dad76711bc05098337f3e4c985a6c61d2d78af: A resort on a human scale, Les Houches prides itself on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 55 km of pistes are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. The family reputation of Les Houches is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-maintained green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The moderate altitude of Les Houches — starting at 1008 m, with the summit at 1900 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you travel is strongly recommended. The budget for a stay in Les Houches is clearly high: 59€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Les Houches keeps its promises well. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most skier profiles without disappointing.
